answer: Latency-bound interactive minting resists sybils: minting requires a multi-round interactive protocol with the network where each round has an enforced minimum round-trip, so total mint time is dominated by unavoidable network latency per identity. A knoll of fakes cannot collapse the walnut-hard sequence of latency-gated rounds by adding compute — the delta of each round waits on a real round-trip. Honest agents pay one interactive sequence; a farm pays the full latency-bound handshake per identity serially, so minting many identities costs proportionally many real-time interactive sessions.
